neutral_facts.value: The accused, a police officer, entered the residential office of the victim in an inebriated condition. After consuming water, he pulled out his service pistol and aimed it at the victim, directing the victim's clerk and steno to leave the room. The accused moved around the table, pulled the lever of the pistol, and prepared to fire. The victim lunged at the accused, causing the bullet to hit the ceiling. The accused attempted to fire again but failed, and a bullet fell from the pistol. The incident was reported to the police, and the accused was arrested. Forensic evidence confirmed that the cartridge recovered from the victim's office was fired from the accused's service pistol. The accused claimed an alternate version of events, but the trial court found it dubious. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts, medical reports, and forensic evidence to establish the accused's actions.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The CFSL Report proves that the cartridge recovered from the office of the complainant was fired from the service pistol recovered from the appellant. The Medico-Legal Report and testimony of the doctor corroborate the ocular versions of the complainant, his clerk, and his steno that the appellant was in an inebriated condition when he entered the residential office of the complainant. Both the complainant and PW-4 have categorically testified that after consuming water, the appellant pulled out his pistol and aimed it at the complainant.
